item.title: Iran war 'close to over', says Trump. Sends 10k new troops
US Senate Republicans reject effort to halt Trump's Iran war
item.description: US Senate Democrats are increasingly divided over arms sales to Israel, with over three dozen backing Bernie Sanders' resolution to halt them. Citing Prime Minister Netanyahu's "reckless decisions" and the expanded conflict, some Democrats shifted their stance. Despite bipartisan opposition, the measures were ultimately rejected, highlighting a growing internal party debate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘End of an era’: Former world No. 1 Jamie Murray, Andy Murray’s brother, retires after 36-year career with seven Grand Slams
item.description: Jamie Murray has retired from professional tennis at 40, concluding a distinguished doubles career spanning over three decades. A former world No. 1, he won seven Grand Slam titles, 34 ATP trophies and played a key role in Britain’s 2015 Davis Cup triumph. Renowned for his longevity and net play, Murray leaves a lasting legacy in British tennis.
item.dc:creator: TOI Sports Desk

item.title: “This is exhausting”: Candace Owens intensifies clash with Erika Kirk after TPUSA event exit as threat claims face public doubt
item.description: Candace Owens publicly challenged Erika Kirk’s claim that security threats forced her to skip a TPUSA event with JD Vance. Owens said the real reason was low ticket sales, while Kirk maintained her decision was based on safety advice. With no confirmed details from either side, the situation has turned into a growing online feud.

item.title: Ironmouse reacts to viral CDawg trampoline moment, educates fans on CVID
item.description: VTuber Ironmouse clarified a viral trampoline video featuring her avatar and CDawgVA, explaining her chronic immune deficiency limits her mobility. The clip, a rare outdoor experience for her, drew criticism. Ironmouse used the moment to raise awareness about CVID and invisible illnesses, highlighting the importance of inclusion and compassion for those with chronic conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Eileen Gu breaks silence on China choice debate, hints at more Olympics while opening up about family loss
item.description: Eileen Gu has once again responded to criticism over representing China, briefly calling it “old news” in an Esquire interview. She earlier reacted to JD Vance with confidence and humor. The 22-year-old also shared plans to continue in future Olympics. Alongside her success, she opened up about the emotional loss of her grandmother during the Winter Games.

item.title: Clavicular breaks silence after overdose scare, addresses viral stream clips
item.description: Kick streamer Braden “Clavicular” has returned to streaming after a viral incident where he appeared unwell and unresponsive during a livestream, leading to hospitalization for a suspected overdose and seizure. He assured fans he is okay but tired, despite medical advice to rest, and plans to continue his work and upcoming club event.

item.title: Olympian Ilona Maher humbled Giants QB Jaxson Dart in a viral moment
item.description: Olympic star Ilona Maher attended a New York Giants party. She did not recognize quarterback Jaxson Dart. Maher asked him about his football team and position. This interaction became a viral sensation. It highlighted Maher's down-to-earth nature. She proved that even famous athletes can be unaware of other sports stars. The event offered a humorous perspective on celebrity recognition.

item.title: Lionel Messi faces fraud lawsuit as Florida promoter alleges huge losses after Argentina star skipped Venezuela exhibition match
item.description: Lionel Messi is facing a lawsuit from Miami company VID over a missed match in 2024. The firm claims it lost over $1 million after Messi did not play against Venezuela despite being fit. The case also involves the Argentine Football Association and follows another recent MLS-related legal settlement involving Messi’s promotional appearances.

item.title: Clavicular situation takes worrying turn after livestream clip spreads and silence raises more concern
item.description: Kick streamer Braden Clavicular was hospitalized on April 14, 2026, after a suspected overdose during a livestream. Viral clips showed him unresponsive at a club. TMZ confirmed the hospitalization, while Taylor Lorenz reported he had a seizure and remains in stable condition but not fully conscious. He is under observation, and no official statement has been released yet.

item.title: EO Charging collapse: Financial strain, global expansion blamed for shutdown
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, EO Charging has shut down its business operations, struggling with the fast-paced global expansion and rising expenses, which have led to significant layoffs. Administrators are currently on hand to aid users during this transitional period.

item.title: El Nino to raise heat: scientists see 0.2°C global rise; UK may face sharper cold
item.description: By the end of 2026, climatologists expect the emergence of El Nino, which may contribute to a rise in global temperatures. While some areas could be flooded with increased rain, others might battle drought and heightened wildfire threats. The UK could be bracing for chillier winters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: World Cup 2026: Is FIFA destroying the American matchday experience by banning tailgating?
item.description: The 2026 World Cup in the United States is reshaping how matchday will be experienced, with traditional tailgating set to be restricted at several venues and fans directed into controlled zones. Combined with rising transport costs and suburban stadium layouts, the pre-match atmosphere faces major disruption, raising questions over how supporter culture will adapt to a tightly managed tournament structure.
